layer.name: Research EMDR layer
layer.position: Established clinical EMDR / supported telehealth / growing group evidence
layer.role: Optional bilateral layer / planned clinician-guided pathway
layer.summary: Clinician-delivered EMDR is an established trauma-focused psychotherapy for PTSD. Individual telehealth delivery is supported and increasingly used, while therapist-led online group G-TEP now has a growing evidence base that includes a 2026 meta-analysis.
layer.boundary: Universal Mind's current bilateral visual and audio feature is an optional research layer, not yet a complete clinical EMDR protocol. Its planned clinician-guided groups of nine are intended as a protocol-governed online group pathway; clinical equivalence depends on clinician governance, protocol fidelity and product-specific outcomes.

heroStudies.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of PTSD
heroStudies.finding: The current U.S. military and veterans guideline places EMDR among the individual trauma-focused psychotherapies with the strongest recommendation for PTSD.
heroStudies.limitation: A clinical guideline for qualified care; it does not validate an entertainment-platform adaptation.

heroStudies.title: Telehealth versus in-person EMDR for veterans
heroStudies.finding: Across 256 veterans, both delivery groups improved. Completion, reliable change and clinically significant change did not differ, although the in-person symptom reduction was larger.
heroStudies.limitation: Treatment format was chosen rather than randomised. This supports individual telehealth delivery; it does not test online group EMDR.

heroStudies.title: Effectiveness of the Group Traumatic Episode Protocol
heroStudies.finding: Twelve G-TEP studies produced a large pooled reduction in PTSD symptoms (Hedges' g=1.28), supporting a feasible group option particularly after collective trauma.
heroStudies.limitation: The synthesis covers G-TEP generally, not online delivery alone or a veterans-only population, and the included methods and samples differed.

heroStudies.title: Video-conference Group EMDR G-TEP for frontline and emergency workers
heroStudies.finding: Eighty-five participants completed a remotely delivered intensive group protocol; PTSD, anxiety and depression measures improved through six-month follow-up.
heroStudies.limitation: The authors call the findings tentative, and no treatment effect was found for moral injury.
